name: APU_1_Authentication
title: APU.1 Authentication (Function)
description: This category is about the system protecting against unauthorized access (e.g., by persons other than the consumer).
purpose:
The functionality of an app, its sponsorship, and linkages to external data sources all affect the security, privacy and data controls which are
established to ensure safe and effective use. In this section, conformance criteria point to issues which can be addressed through a range of options, and
as such implementers should consider not only the conformance criteria but the discussion regarding applicability to the exemplary use cases.

statement.label: APU.1#01
statement.requirement: The system SHALL authenticate the identity of a user prior to any access to PHI or PII.

statement.label: APU.1#02
statement.requirement: The system SHALL communicate the method of authentication to the user when an account is established.

statement.label: APU.1#03
statement.requirement: The system SHALL authorize the user to access a feature before that feature or any associated PHI or PII is displayed. Authorization may be internal to the system or derived from an external source.

statement.label: APU.1#04
statement.requirement: The system SHALL terminate, at the request of a user, such that subsequent access to PHI or PII requires a new, successful authentication attempt.

statement.label: APU.1#05
statement.requirement: IF another external health IT system, such as an EHR, is a system actor THEN the system SHALL verify a subject's association with their real-world identity, establishing that the subject is who they claim to be (identity proofing).

statement.label: APU.1#06
statement.requirement: IF an EHR is a system actor THEN the system SHALL ensure that the EHR authorizes the user's access to those system features that are supported by data provided by, or written to, the EHR.

statement.label: APU.1#07
statement.requirement: IF PII or PHI are displayed THEN the system SHALL terminate, or make PHI and PII invisible, after a period of user inactivity as described in its Terms of Use. This feature is sometimes called inactivity timeout, session timeout, or automatic logoff. The decision to include this feature is made as part of the overall risk analysis regarding the sensitivity of the data provided by or through the system.

statement.label: APU.1#08
statement.requirement: IF passwords are stored on the device THEN the system SHALL encrypt those passwords and SHALL NOT display them as plaintext.

statement.label: APU.1#09
statement.requirement: IF access to an account exposes Protected Health Information (PHI) or PII THEN the system SHALL give the user the option to use strong authentication methods, such as multi-factor authentication or biometrics, in addition to passwords. Before the user selects this option, the system clearly describes or demonstrates the authentication mechanism. This capability may apply to the system itself and to the pairing of the system with a device.

statement.label: APU.1#10
statement.requirement: IF an AI component can access PHI, PII, credentials, or an external system on behalf of a user THEN the system SHALL ensure that the AI component receives only the least-privileged, time-limited access necessary for the authorized task and SHALL prevent the AI component from exposing authentication secrets, tokens, or credentials in consumer-visible output or logs.

statement.label: APU.1#11
statement.requirement: IF an AI-enabled function can execute an external action or disclose new data THEN the system SHOULD require re-authentication or another strong confirmation before the action is completed when the risk assessment identifies a meaningful risk of harm, disclosure, or irreversible change.
